text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government not prepared to continue propping up Malta Drydocks at present rate, says Prime Minister Alfred Sant. Malta Drydocks was being supported by Lm15 million (about $40 million) per year, the equivalent of five new schools. The dockyard has accumulated losses of $220 million.
- German tourist lifted by helicopter after falling down a cliff. She suffered fractures.

- Opposition leader Edward Fenech Adami says government policies could lead to recession. He said the government needed to invest and should not have a policy of just making do. He also hit out at the government for stopping Malta's application to join the European Union.
- Prime Minister Alfred Sant says his government inherited disaster in public finance. The extent of the deficit would be made known when the budget was presented on Monday evening.
